page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized server built on x86_64 architecture using AMD EPYC 9B14 processors. The instance provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM, resulting in a ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core. Cache specifications include 32 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction set extensions feature AVX-512 vector instructions (f, vnni, bf16), AES, VAES, and SHA_NI hardware acceleration. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or GPU hardware.

Performance data indicates high single-core CPU throughput, ranking in the top 25% on stress-ng single-thread benchmarks. Single-threaded text processing, bzip3 decompression, and gzip compression show mid-range results. In contrast, multi-core CPU scoring and total memory bandwidth drop into the lower 25th percentile. Memory benchmark tests report limited throughput during large-block read and write operations, which correlates with low scores in memory-sensitive workloads including Redis operation rates, static web serving throughput, and PassMark database tests.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a lean hardware configuration designed to minimize memory allocation overhead for CPU-heavy tasks. However, the low memory capacity limits parallel scaling for data-heavy operations. The instance is suited for single-threaded compute tasks, utility scripting, lightweight batch processing, and low-concurrency application services that do not require high memory bandwidth or local SSD storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor on x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs spanning 2 physical cores with hyperthreading and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX-512, AES, and SHA vector instructions, with cache allocation comprising 32 MB L3 cache. Benchmarks show strong single-core CPU performance in the top quartile, alongside average execution times for single-threaded compression and general CPU benchmarks. Conversely, multi-core throughput, memory bandwidth, and database transaction rates fall into the bottom quartile due to low memory density and limited memory bus transfer speeds. The instance offers resource efficiency for compute-heavy, low-memory execution paths without bundled local disk or GPU accelerators. It is suitable for batch processing, basic text processing, utility scripts, and single-threaded compute workloads.
